value.rationale: For the exact maps used to demonstrate that mixing singular deterministic dynamics can produce Lebesgue stationarity, determining the full set of stationary randomization protocols is a natural classification problem. A fixed spatial law and identically distributed independent map-choice labels do not identify even the sign/size of a two-time stationary correlation; the full sharp, attained rational covariance interval (length 23/512 in the source example) quantifies a consequential temporal nonidentifiability with no arbitrary truncation or unmotivated sample-size choice. The extremal protocols are constructive for all allowed parameters. The result is self-contained and is not framed as a global ergodic or independence theorem for coordinates.
